executive.name: Office of the CEO & Strategy
executive.description: Executive leadership, strategic direction, governance, board relations and high-level decision making.
executive.charter: Set organizational purpose, allocate strategic capital, and own cross-functional escalation.

corporate-strategy.name: Corporate Strategy
corporate-strategy.description: Long-range strategic planning, M&A, competitive intelligence, and market positioning.
corporate-strategy.charter: Analyze competitive dynamics, assess industry disruption, and drive strategic portfolio choices.

technology.name: Technology & Engineering
technology.description: Software engineering, system architecture, DevOps, APIs, and cloud infrastructure.
technology.charter: Design, build, deploy, and maintain robust, scalable and secure technological systems.

it-operations.name: IT Operations & Infrastructure
it-operations.description: Internal systems, enterprise IT tooling, workstation management, and network availability.
it-operations.charter: Ensure operational uptime, seamless internal toolchains, and employee technological support.

product.name: Product Management
product.description: Product discovery, roadmap prioritization, feature specification, and UX alignment.
product.charter: Translate customer problems and strategic goals into delightful, viable product experiences.

security.name: Information Security (SecOps)
security.description: Cybersecurity, threat modeling, vulnerability management, compliance (SOC2/ISO27001) and incident response.
security.charter: Protect organizational assets, enforce zero-trust posture, and maintain security hygiene.

data-analytics.name: Data & Analytics
data-analytics.description: Business intelligence, data pipelines, warehousing, metric modeling, and predictive analytics.
data-analytics.charter: Transform raw operational data into trusted, actionable decision support models.

marketing.name: Brand & Product Marketing
marketing.description: Brand narrative, positioning, creative direction, design systems, and market messaging.
marketing.charter: Establish unmistakable brand identity and communicate value clearly to target markets.

demand-generation.name: Demand Generation & Growth
demand-generation.description: Paid media, SEO, performance marketing, content syndication, and inbound acquisition funnels.
demand-generation.charter: Generate sustainable, predictable pipeline of qualified leads and customers.

revenue.name: Revenue & Sales
revenue.description: Enterprise sales, sales engineering, pricing strategy, pipeline velocity, and revenue ops.
revenue.charter: Close revenue predictably, maximize contract values, and optimize sales cycles.

customer-experience.name: Customer Experience & Success
customer-experience.description: Onboarding, retention, customer support, NPS, churn prevention, and account expansion.
customer-experience.charter: Ensure customer value realization, minimize churn, and drive lifetime advocacy.

finance.name: Finance & Accounting
finance.description: Budgeting, financial forecasting, FP&A, treasury, unit economics, and accounting controls.
finance.charter: Maintain financial integrity, optimize capital runway, and ensure accurate fiscal reporting.

operations.name: Business Operations
operations.description: Process optimization, workflow automation, operational cadence, and vendor procurement.
operations.charter: Remove cross-functional friction and ensure reliable daily business execution.

pmo.name: Program Management Office (PMO)
pmo.description: Cross-functional initiative tracking, delivery milestones, dependency management, and project reporting.
pmo.charter: Keep complex multi-team initiatives on schedule, on budget, and unblocked.

people.name: People & Talent (HR)
people.description: Talent acquisition, organizational design, culture, career progression, and performance reviews.
people.charter: Attract, develop, and retain the highest-performing workforce while fostering healthy culture.

legal-risk.name: Legal, Compliance & Risk
legal-risk.description: Commercial contracts, IP protection, regulatory compliance (LGPD/GDPR), and liability management.
legal-risk.charter: Shield the enterprise from legal liability while enabling commercial velocity.

skills.name: chief-strategy-officer
skills.description: Owns where the business plays and how it wins over a multi-year horizon — portfolio choices, corporate development, strategic partnerships, and planning under uncertainty. Use this for a decision about which markets or businesses to be in, whether to build, buy, or partner, how to allocate capital across business lines, or when a long-horizon bet needs framing. Distinct from `chief-executive`, which arbitrates present-quarter conflicts.

skills.name: market-entry
skills.description: Decides whether and how to enter a new market — sizing demand from the bottom up rather than from a market report, testing whether your advantage transfers, choosing between organic entry, partnership and acquisition, sequencing the operational and regulatory work that entry actually requires, and setting the criteria that would tell you to stop. Use this to evaluate a new geography, segment or vertical, pressure-test an entry plan, or work out why a launched market never reached scale.

skills.name: mergers-and-acquisitions
skills.description: Runs corporate development — deal thesis, target screening, valuation framing, diligence, and integration planning. Use this when considering an acquisition or being approached about one, when evaluating build-versus-buy at company scale, when running or reviewing diligence, or when planning how an acquired business will actually be integrated.

skills.name: portfolio-strategy
skills.description: Decides where capital and attention go across business lines, products, and markets — what to fund, hold, harvest, or exit, and on what evidence. Use this to allocate budget across businesses, evaluate whether a product line should continue, decide whether to exit one, structure a portfolio review, or when several initiatives compete for the same limited investment.

skills.name: scenario-planning
skills.description: Plans under genuine uncertainty — building scenarios, identifying which assumptions are load-bearing, setting early-warning indicators, and stress-testing a plan against futures rather than forecasting one. Use this when a decision depends on something unknowable, when a plan assumes conditions that may not hold, before a large irreversible commitment, or when a market, regulatory, or technology shift could invalidate the strategy.

skills.name: strategic-alliances
skills.description: Structures partnerships that change what the business can do — technology integrations, channel and reseller arrangements, joint ventures, and OEM relationships. Use this to evaluate or structure a strategic partnership, decide between partnering and building, negotiate commercial terms of an alliance, or diagnose a partnership that is signed but not producing. For audience-borrowing partnerships, use `marketing:partnership-marketing`.

skills.name: chief-customer-officer
skills.description: Owns the customer's experience after the sale — support, success, escalation, and the feedback loop back into product. Use this for a decision spanning support and product, when service quality and cost are in tension, when deciding what to staff or automate, when a customer relationship is at risk above the account-manager level, or when nobody owns a recurring customer problem.

skills.name: customer-onboarding-and-implementation
skills.description: Takes a new customer from signature to working — setting a definition of live that both sides agreed before the contract was signed, planning and staffing the implementation, running data migration and integration realistically, training the people who will actually use it, and handing over to the ongoing relationship. Use this to design an onboarding motion, rescue a stalled implementation, work out why customers who bought never went live, or scope the services a deal actually needs.

skills.name: customer-success-management
skills.description: Runs the ongoing relationship with accounts after the sale — segmenting coverage against account value, building a health score that predicts rather than describes, running reviews customers find worth attending, forecasting renewals honestly, and finding expansion that follows usage instead of quota. Use this to design a customer success motion, decide who gets a named contact, work out why renewals surprise you, or fix a health score everyone ignores.

skills.name: escalation-management
skills.description: Handles customer situations that have exceeded normal support — severity assessment, incident communication, executive escalation, and recovering a relationship after a failure. Use this when a customer issue is escalating or has gone to leadership, during a customer-affecting outage, when a major account is at risk, when a relationship needs repairing after a failure, or to design the escalation path itself.

skills.name: self-service-and-knowledge
skills.description: Builds the help center, in-product guidance, and knowledge base that let customers resolve problems without contacting anyone — content, findability, maintenance, and deflection measurement. Use this to build or fix a help center, reduce support volume, write documentation for customers, improve findability, or decide what deserves a help article versus a product fix.

skills.name: support-operations
skills.description: Designs and runs the support function — channels, queues, routing, staffing, service levels, quality, and the metrics that show whether it is working. Use this to set up or fix support operations, choose channels, size a team, set or renegotiate service levels, reduce cost per contact, diagnose long queues or poor quality, or decide what to automate.

skills.name: voice-of-customer
skills.description: Builds the loop from what customers say to what gets changed — collecting feedback, distinguishing signal from noise, routing it to owners, and closing the loop back to the customer. Use this to set up a feedback program, design or interpret CSAT/NPS, decide what customer feedback deserves action, get product to act on recurring issues, or diagnose why feedback is collected but nothing changes.

skills.name: ai-ml-governance
skills.description: Governs models and AI systems in production — intended use, evaluation, monitoring, human oversight, documentation, and the decision to deploy or retire. Use this before deploying a model or AI feature, when defining evaluation criteria, when a model's behavior has drifted, when assessing AI risk or regulatory exposure, or when deciding whether an AI system is fit for a consequential decision.

skills.name: business-intelligence
skills.description: Builds reporting and self-serve analytics that people actually use — metric trees, dashboard design, distribution, and the discipline that stops dashboards proliferating. Use this to build a dashboard or report, design a metrics framework, set up self-serve analytics, decide what to measure, or diagnose why reporting exists but nobody uses it or trusts it.

skills.name: chief-data-officer
skills.description: Owns data as an asset — governance, quality, the warehouse and semantic layer, analytics capability, and the governance of models built on top. Use this for a decision about how data is collected, stored, defined, or shared; when numbers disagree between teams; when deciding what to build in-house versus buy; when standing up a data function; or when an AI or model decision needs governance rather than engineering.

skills.name: data-engineering
skills.description: Builds and operates data pipelines — ingestion, transformation, orchestration, quality testing, and reliability of data delivery. Use this to design or debug a pipeline, decide batch versus streaming, add data quality checks, handle late or duplicate data, or work out why a dashboard's numbers changed without anyone changing the dashboard.

skills.name: data-governance
skills.description: Establishes ownership, definitions, quality, access, and lineage for the organization's data. Use this when metrics disagree between teams, when nobody knows which dataset is authoritative, when setting up data ownership or access policy, when data quality is unreliable, or before opening a dataset to a wider audience.

skills.name: data-modeling
skills.description: Designs the warehouse and semantic layer — source-to-mart structure, dimensional modeling, grain, slowly changing dimensions, and the metric layer analytics reads through. Use this to design or restructure a warehouse, model a new source, decide on grain or table structure, build a semantic or metric layer, or diagnose why queries are slow, wrong, or impossible to write.

skills.name: quantitative-analysis
skills.description: Answers a business question with data without fooling yourself — framing the question so an answer would change something, choosing the right comparison, checking the data before trusting it, recognizing the traps that produce confident wrong answers (aggregation reversals, survivorship, regression to the mean, multiple comparisons), and reporting uncertainty honestly. Use this to run an analysis, review one before acting on it, or work out why two people looking at the same data reached opposite conclusions.

skills.name: account-based-marketing
skills.description: Concentrates marketing and sales effort on a named set of accounts rather than on volume — qualifying whether the model fits your economics at all, building the account list and the buying group inside each, tiering effort against account value, coordinating so the account experiences one campaign rather than several, and measuring account progression instead of leads. Use this to decide whether to run an account-based program, build one, or work out why an existing one produces activity and no pipeline.

skills.name: ai-search-optimization
skills.description: Optimizes for AI assistants and AI-generated answers — being retrievable, being cited, and being represented accurately when a model answers on your behalf. Use this when traffic is shifting from links to AI answers, when a brand is misrepresented or absent in AI responses, when planning content for retrieval rather than ranking, or when deciding how AI search changes an existing SEO program.

skills.name: app-store-optimization
skills.description: Improves visibility and conversion in the App Store and Google Play — metadata, keywords, screenshots, ratings, and the listing experience that turns an impression into an install. Use this to audit or optimize an app listing, plan a launch listing, diagnose poor install conversion, or improve store search visibility.

skills.name: experimentation
skills.description: Designs, runs, and reads A/B tests and growth experiments — hypothesis, sample size, duration, and honest interpretation. Use this to plan a test, judge whether a result is real, build an experimentation program, decide what to test next, or diagnose why tests keep producing inconclusive or non-replicating results.

skills.name: landing-page-cro-expert
skills.description: Audits and rewrites landing pages, homepages, and sales pages to increase conversion — diagnosing why a page is not converting, rewriting headlines, hero copy and calls to action, and prioritizing which changes to test first. Use this when a page underperforms, when someone pastes a URL or screenshot asking what is wrong, when writing a new page, or when deciding which conversion changes are worth testing.

skills.name: lead-capture
skills.description: Converts anonymous traffic into known contacts — lead magnets, gated content, free tools, popups, and the forms behind them. Use this to design or improve a lead magnet, plan a free tool, add or fix popups and overlays, improve form conversion, or decide what is worth gating and what should stay open.

skills.name: lifecycle-messaging
skills.description: Designs automated email and SMS programs — welcome and onboarding sequences, nurture, re-engagement, transactional messaging, and the timing and segmentation behind them. Use this to build or fix an email sequence, plan lifecycle automation, improve open or click performance, set up SMS flows, or decide what messages a customer should receive and when.

skills.name: listing-distribution
skills.description: Gets a product listed where buyers and crawlers look — directories, marketplaces, review sites, comparison pages, and aggregators. Use this to plan a submission push, choose which directories are worth the effort, prepare listing assets, build comparison and alternative pages, or manage presence on review platforms.

skills.name: marketing-analytics
skills.description: Sets up, audits, and reports on marketing measurement — tracking plans, event schemas, attribution models, and the dashboards built on them. Use this to instrument a site or product, audit tracking nobody trusts, choose or interpret an attribution model, build reporting that answers a specific question, or reconcile numbers that disagree between tools.

skills.name: paid-advertising
skills.description: Plans, runs, and optimizes paid acquisition across search, social, and display — account structure, targeting, creative, bidding, budget, and the analysis that says whether to scale or stop. Use this to set up or restructure campaigns, write and iterate ad creative, diagnose rising costs or falling performance, decide budget allocation, or judge whether a channel is working.

skills.name: programmatic-seo
skills.description: Builds large sets of search-targeted pages from a template and a dataset — the location, comparison, integration, and use-case pages that capture long-tail demand at scale. Use this when there is a repeating query pattern with real volume, when a dataset could answer many similar searches, or to judge whether a programmatic approach is viable before building it.

skills.name: seo-strategy
skills.description: Audits and improves organic search performance — technical health, site architecture, internal linking, structured data, and the content decisions that determine what can rank. Use this to run an SEO audit, diagnose why pages are not ranking or were deindexed, plan a site's URL and navigation structure, add structured data, or prioritize which SEO fixes are worth doing.

skills.name: agent-hierarchy
skills.description: Designs orchestrator-and-subagent hierarchies for a repository — splitting agents by exclusive write surface, pairing every producer with an independent auditor, and enforcing the split with a script that runs in CI. Use this whenever the user wants to set up, expand, audit, or fix a multi-agent or subagent structure for a codebase; asks how to divide work between agents; wants agent charters, roles, or a surface map written; or is hitting agents that collide on the same files, review their own work, or drift from their remit. Also use when sizing a roster or deciding whether a new agent is justified.

skills.name: ai-research-analyst
skills.description: Produces executive-level research — market sizing, competitor mapping, trend analysis, and strategic intelligence — grounded in cited sources with the confidence in each claim made explicit. Use this to analyze a market or industry, map competitors, evaluate a market-entry or build-versus-buy decision, produce a research brief, or assemble evidence for a decision. Also use when comparing options that need a structured, evidence-based verdict rather than an opinion.

skills.name: business-growth-consultant
skills.description: Finds the single constraint currently limiting a business's growth and the highest-leverage moves against it, rather than producing a list of everything that could be improved. Use this when growth has stalled or slowed, when deciding where to spend limited time or budget, when revenue rises but profit does not, when prioritizing growth initiatives, or when a business feels busy without compounding.

skills.name: ceo-advisor
skills.description: Pressure-tests a decision, plan, or idea before it is committed to — surfacing the assumption it rests on, the case against it, and what would have to be true for it to work. Use this when weighing options, when a plan needs challenging before commitment, when you have already decided and want a genuine gut check, when processing meeting notes into decisions, or when competing initiatives need ranking. Distinct from `chief-executive`, which owns direction; this one interrogates a specific decision.

skills.name: chief-executive
skills.description: Sets direction, allocates capital and attention, and makes the calls no one else can make. Use this when a decision spans more than one function, when priorities conflict and something must be cut, when a plan needs pressure-testing before commitment, or when the question is what the organization should do rather than how to do it. Also use to route a request to the right executive when it is unclear who owns it.

skills.name: fundraising-and-investor-relations
skills.description: Raises capital and manages the relationship afterward — deciding how much and why, understanding what dilution and preferences actually cost, running a process with real competitive tension, preparing for diligence before it starts, and reporting to investors and a board in a way that keeps support when results are bad. Use this to plan a raise, evaluate a term sheet beyond the valuation, prepare a data room, or fix reporting that is producing surprises.

skills.name: saas-idea-validator
skills.description: Evaluates a software or startup idea against problem, market, competition, monetization, defensibility, and execution, and returns a verdict rather than encouragement. Use this when an idea needs pressure-testing before anyone builds, when deciding whether something is worth pursuing, when assessing competition or willingness to pay, or when a validated idea needs a first-customers and MVP plan. Default to scrutiny; the useful answer is usually the unwelcome one.

skills.name: budgeting-and-forecasting
skills.description: Runs the planning cycle — annual budget, rolling forecast, consolidation of business unit inputs, and the variance analysis that explains actuals against plan. Use this to build or challenge a budget, run a forecast cycle, consolidate departmental submissions, explain why results diverged from plan, or improve forecast accuracy.

skills.name: capital-allocation
skills.description: Evaluates where to spend limited capital — investment appraisal, hurdle rates, payback, and comparing proposals that are not alike. Use this to evaluate an investment or major purchase, compare competing funding requests, set a hurdle rate, decide between building and buying, or review whether past investments delivered what was claimed.

skills.name: capital-structure-and-covenants
skills.description: Decides how the business is financed and what that financing then requires of it — debt versus equity, weighted average cost of capital as a hurdle rate, how much leverage cash flow can carry, and the financial, affirmative and negative covenants, definitions, test dates and cure rights that come attached. Use this to evaluate a financing option, set an investment hurdle, check whether a planned decision will trip a covenant, or work out what a lender can do when one breaks.

skills.name: chief-financial-officer
skills.description: Owns the financial position: planning, budgeting, forecasting, unit economics, cash, and the numbers the business is run and reported on. Use this to build or challenge a budget, model a decision's financial consequence, assess unit economics or runway, evaluate an investment or spend request, set financial controls, or when a plan's numbers do not reconcile. Also use to decide whether the business can afford something.

skills.name: cost-accounting
skills.description: Establishes what something actually costs — fixed, variable and mixed cost behavior, absorption versus variable costing, job-order, process and activity-based methods, breakeven and operating leverage, and price/volume/mix decomposition. Use this to set a price floor, explain why revenue or margin moved, decide make versus buy, judge whether a product line earns its place, or work out how an allocation basis is distorting a reported margin.

skills.name: financial-modeling
skills.description: Builds and stress-tests financial models for forecasting, scenario planning, and decision support — revenue build, cost structure, driver logic, and the sensitivities that show where a plan breaks. Use this to model a decision's financial consequence, build a forecast or long-range plan, evaluate an investment or hire, or pressure-test someone else's model before relying on it.

skills.name: financial-reporting-and-close
skills.description: Runs the period-end close and produces reporting — close calendar, reconciliations, accruals, variance analysis, and reporting that gets read. Use this to shorten or stabilize a monthly close, design a close checklist, investigate a variance, structure management reporting, or work out why the numbers keep changing after close.

skills.name: financial-statement-analysis
skills.description: Reads a set of financial statements and establishes what changed and why — fluctuation analysis against prior period and against budget, profitability, liquidity, solvency and efficiency ratios, benchmarking, and the non-GAAP measures presented alongside them. Use this to interpret results, review a counterparty's or target's financials, diagnose a deteriorating trend, explain a variance to someone who will act on it, or test whether an adjusted number is honest.

skills.name: internal-controls-and-audit
skills.description: Designs and tests controls over financial reporting — segregation of duties, approval limits, evidence, and preparing for audit. Use this to design controls for a process, prepare for an external audit, respond to an audit finding, set approval thresholds, or assess where a small team's segregation of duties is genuinely broken.

skills.name: revenue-recognition
skills.description: Determines when and how revenue is recognized — performance obligations, contract terms that change the answer, and the deal structures that create accounting problems. Use this to work out how a contract should be recognized, review a non-standard deal before it is signed, understand deferred revenue, or spot terms that would delay or reverse recognition.

skills.name: tax
skills.description: Structures the tax questions a growing business faces — corporate income, sales and use, payroll, nexus, and the obligations created by hiring or selling somewhere new. Use this to work out what a new state or country obligates you to, prepare for a tax filing or audit, understand sales tax on your product, or check what a remote hire or new market triggers.

skills.name: treasury-and-liquidity
skills.description: Manages cash and liquidity — cash forecasting, runway, working capital, banking structure, and currency and counterparty exposure. Use this to build a cash forecast, extend runway, improve working capital, decide where cash should sit, or assess exposure to a bank, currency, or customer concentration.

skills.name: unit-economics
skills.description: Establishes whether the business makes money on each customer or unit — contribution margin, acquisition cost, payback period, lifetime value, and the cohort behavior underneath. Use this to assess whether growth is profitable, evaluate a channel or segment, support a pricing decision, judge how fast the business can afford to grow, or diagnose why revenue growth is not producing profit.

skills.name: backup-and-recovery
skills.description: Protects and restores data — backup coverage and scope, retention, immutability against ransomware, and proving restores actually work. Use this to design a backup regime, verify restores, plan retention, protect backups from ransomware, or recover from data loss.

skills.name: chief-information-officer
skills.description: The CIO's remit — running the technology the company works on, service quality, IT spend, and the boundary with product engineering. Use this to set IT priorities, decide what IT owns versus engineering, structure IT spend or an IT roadmap, judge whether to build, buy or outsource, or work out why IT is seen as a cost center rather than an enabler.

skills.name: cloud-administration
skills.description: Administers the cloud the company runs on rather than the one it sells — tenant and subscription structure, the SaaS estate and who owns each app, identity as the real perimeter, cloud spend that arrives as a surprise, and what the provider does not do for you. Use this to structure subscriptions or tenants, get control of sprawling SaaS, cut a cloud bill, work out who owns an application nobody admits to buying, or decide what corporate workloads belong in cloud at all.

skills.name: collaboration-platform-administration
skills.description: Administers the email, chat, meeting and file-sharing platform the organization runs on — tenant and domain configuration, mail authentication and routing, phishing and spam controls, shared mailboxes and distribution groups, external sharing and guest access, permission sprawl in file storage, and retention and legal hold. Use this to configure a tenant, tighten sharing, investigate a mail delivery or phishing problem, or work out who can see a file and why.

skills.name: endpoint-management
skills.description: Manages laptops, desktops and mobile devices — enrollment, configuration, patching, software distribution, and lost or compromised devices. Use this to set up device management, standardize builds, roll out software or an OS upgrade, handle a lost device, or bring an unmanaged fleet under control.

skills.name: identity-lifecycle-administration
skills.description: Executes joiner, mover and leaver processes — provisioning, group membership, access changes on role change, and complete deprovisioning. Use this to set up or fix joiner-mover-leaver, deprovision someone completely, clean up accumulated access, audit group membership, or find accounts that outlived their owners.

skills.name: it-asset-management
skills.description: Tracks hardware and software assets through their life — procurement, ownership, licensing, refresh, and disposal. Use this to build an asset register, prepare for a software audit, plan a refresh cycle, control license spend, or dispose of equipment safely.

skills.name: network-administration
skills.description: Designs and operates the corporate network — segmentation, remote access, wireless, DNS and addressing, and diagnosing network problems. Use this to segment a network, set up or fix remote access, diagnose intermittent connectivity, plan addressing or DNS, or assess whether the network's trust assumptions still hold.

skills.name: service-desk
skills.description: Runs the IT service desk — intake, triage, prioritization, escalation, knowledge, and the metrics that improve service rather than distort it. Use this to set up or fix a service desk, design ticket priority and escalation, reduce repeat contacts, structure a knowledge base, or work out why a desk hitting its targets still frustrates everyone.

skills.name: systems-administration
skills.description: Runs servers and corporate systems — patching, configuration baselines, change control, capacity, and the routine that prevents incidents. Use this to establish a patching cadence, standardize server configuration, plan a maintenance window, decide change control for infrastructure, or clean up systems that have drifted from any known state.

skills.name: telephony-and-conferencing
skills.description: Runs voice and meeting infrastructure — phone systems and numbers, emergency calling obligations, conference rooms and their AV, call recording and its retention consequences, and the porting that makes provider changes go badly. Use this to replace a phone system, fix rooms nobody can start a meeting in, meet emergency-calling requirements, port numbers without losing service, or work out why voice quality degrades only sometimes.

skills.name: virtualization-operations
skills.description: Runs the hypervisor layer beneath the servers — host capacity and consolidation ratios, VM sprawl, snapshot discipline, resilience and live migration, and licensing that counts cores rather than instances. Use this to size or expand a cluster, work out why VMs are slow when the hosts look idle, clean up sprawl, set snapshot and template policy, or decide what stays virtualized and what moves to cloud.

skills.name: chief-legal-and-risk-officer
skills.description: Owns legal, contracts, intellectual property, regulatory compliance, privacy, security governance, enterprise risk, and audit readiness. Use this to review a contract or commitment, assess regulatory or privacy exposure, evaluate an IP or licensing question, judge the risk in a business decision, prepare for an audit or certification, or when a plan may create obligations the business cannot meet. Also use to decide whether a risk should be accepted, mitigated, or refused.

skills.name: contract-review
skills.description: Reviews and negotiates commercial agreements — MSAs, SOWs, order forms, NDAs, vendor and data-processing agreements — identifying material risk, proposing positions, and recommending a path rather than listing issues. Use this to review a contract before signature, prepare a negotiation position, build fallback positions and approval thresholds, or assess exposure in terms already agreed.

skills.name: corporate-governance
skills.description: Maintains the corporate record and the governance machinery — entity records, board and committee support, resolutions and minutes, delegations of authority, insurance, and business continuity. Use this to prepare board or committee materials, record a decision that needs to be minuted, set or check approval authority, review insurance and continuity coverage, establish a retention policy, or work out where a responsibility belongs when it falls between functions.

skills.name: disputes-and-legal-holds
skills.description: Handles a dispute from the first sign of it — recognizing when preservation obligations attach, issuing and scoping a legal hold, suspending automatic deletion across every system that holds relevant material, preserving privilege, managing outside counsel and cost, and evaluating settlement against the real cost of continuing. Use this to respond to a claim or demand letter, issue a hold, work out which systems the hold has to reach, or decide whether to fight.

skills.name: enterprise-risk
skills.description: Identifies, assesses, and tracks organizational risk — building and maintaining a risk register, scoring exposure, assigning owners and treatments, and preparing for audit. Use this to stand up a risk program, assess the risk in a decision or initiative, prepare for a certification or audit, decide whether a risk should be accepted, mitigated, transferred, or avoided, or report risk posture to leadership.

skills.name: intellectual-property
skills.description: Covers what the organization owns and what it is only borrowing — trademarks and clearance, copyright and work-for-hire, patents and trade secrets, open-source license obligations and copyleft reach, and IP terms in customer, contractor and AI-tool agreements. Use this to check whether a name is usable, establish that you own work you paid for, decide how to handle a license obligation in a dependency, or respond to an infringement claim.

skills.name: privacy-and-data-protection
skills.description: Assesses and improves how personal data is collected, used, shared, and retained — data mapping, lawful basis, consent, processor agreements, subject rights, and breach obligations. Use this before launching anything that handles personal data, when adding a vendor that will process it, when a data subject request arrives, when assessing exposure under GDPR or US state privacy laws, or when preparing for a privacy review.

skills.name: regulatory-compliance
skills.description: Identifies which regulations apply and builds the program that keeps you inside them — obligation mapping, controls, monitoring, and responding to regulators. Use this to work out what applies to your business, stand up a compliance program, prepare for a regulatory exam or certification, respond to a finding, or assess exposure before entering a new market.

skills.name: behavioral-marketing
skills.description: Applies decision science and cognitive bias research to marketing and product decisions — how people actually choose under uncertainty, and how framing, defaults, sequencing, and social context change behavior. Use this to diagnose why a well-argued offer is not converting, to structure choices and pricing presentation, to design an experience around how attention and memory work, or to pressure-test whether a persuasion tactic is legitimate or manipulative.

skills.name: brand-voice
skills.description: Captures how a person or brand actually writes and turns it into reusable voice instructions every other content skill draws from. skills.name: code-review
skills.description: Conducts and responds to code review — reviewing a change for correctness, design, and risk, and evaluating review feedback received on your own work. Use this before merging, when asked to review a diff or pull request, when review feedback has arrived and needs acting on, or when feedback seems wrong and needs a reasoned response rather than compliance.

skills.name: completion-verification
skills.description: Verifies that work is actually complete before it is claimed to be — running the checks, reading the output, and confirming the original request was satisfied rather than approximated. Use this before saying something is done, fixed, or passing; before committing or opening a pull request; and whenever a claim of success has not been backed by command output.

skills.name: data-migration
skills.description: Moves data from one system to another without losing it or corrupting it — profiling the source before mapping, deciding between big-bang and parallel-run cutover, reconciling counts and values rather than assuming, handling the records that will not map cleanly, and planning a rollback that is actually executable. Use this to plan or run a migration, assess a migration plan someone else wrote, work out why a completed migration is producing wrong numbers, or size how long one will really take.

skills.name: implementation-planning
skills.description: Turns a spec or requirement into a written plan a separate session or agent can execute, then drives that plan through review checkpoints. Use this before touching code on any multi-step task, when work needs handing to someone else, when a task keeps sprawling mid-implementation, or when a plan exists and needs executing in order with verification between steps.

skills.name: observability-and-reliability
skills.description: Makes systems debuggable and reliably operable — instrumentation, alerting that is worth waking for, service objectives, and learning from failure. Use this to instrument a service, fix alerting that is ignored, set error budgets or reliability targets, prepare for on-call, or run a blameless post-incident review.

skills.name: parallel-agent-delivery
skills.description: Splits work across multiple agents or sessions running at once, keeping their surfaces disjoint so results merge cleanly. Use this when facing several independent tasks with no shared state, when a plan has parallelizable steps, when a broad search or audit would be faster fanned out, or when deciding whether work can safely be split at all.

skills.name: prompt-optimizer
skills.description: Turns rough intent or a weak prompt into a reliable one — diagnosing why output is inconsistent, restructuring the instruction, and adapting it across models. Use this when a prompt is not producing what was wanted, when output varies run to run, when writing a prompt for a repeated task, when moving a prompt between models, or when someone describes what they want an AI to do and needs it written properly.

skills.name: release-and-deployment
skills.description: Ships changes safely and often — pipelines, deployment strategies, feature flags, rollback, and database changes. Use this to design a deployment pipeline, reduce release risk, roll out a risky change gradually, plan a schema migration, or work out why releases are infrequent and frightening.

skills.name: skill-authoring
skills.description: Writes and revises agent skills so they trigger at the right moments and give usable instruction when they do. Use this when creating a new skill, editing an existing one, diagnosing a skill that fires too often or never fires, or reviewing a set of skills for overlap. Also use before adding to a skill library, to check the capability is not already covered.

skills.name: solution-architecture
skills.description: Designs system structure and makes architectural decisions defensible — boundaries, coupling, trade-offs, and recording why. Use this to design a new system or major component, choose between architectural options, review an existing design, decide where a boundary belongs, or document an architectural decision so it survives the people who made it.

skills.name: solution-exploration
skills.description: Explores the problem and the range of possible approaches before any code is written — clarifying what is actually being asked, surfacing options with their tradeoffs, and converging on one. Use this at the start of any feature, component, or behavior change, when a request is ambiguous, when the first idea is the only idea on the table, or when a design decision needs pressure-testing before commitment.

skills.name: systematic-debugging
skills.description: Finds the root cause of a bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior before proposing any fix. Use this whenever something is broken and the cause is not yet proven — a failing test, a production error, intermittent behavior, or a symptom that appeared after a change. Also use when a fix has been attempted and did not work, or when the same bug keeps coming back.

skills.name: technical-debt-management
skills.description: Makes technical debt visible and decidable — distinguishing real debt from mess, quantifying its cost, and arguing for remediation in business terms. Use this to assess and prioritize debt, decide whether to fix or live with something, justify remediation work to non-engineers, or plan a migration off a system nobody wants to touch.

skills.name: test-driven-development
skills.description: Drives implementation by writing a failing test first, then the smallest code that passes it. Use this before writing implementation code for any feature or bugfix, when a bug needs a regression test, when existing code is hard to change safely, or when someone asks whether a change is covered. Also use to decide what is worth testing and what is not.

skills.name: apresentacao-e-slide-deck-sobre-ia
skills.description: Criar a estrutura completa de apresentações sobre IA agêntica na educação — com narrativa, roteiro de cada slide, textos de apoio e notas do apresentador — para que o creator transforme seu conhecimento em palestras, aulas ou pitches que impressionam pela clareza e pela profundidade, sem precisar montar o deck do zero toda vez.

skills.name: artigo-de-autoridade-para-linkedin
skills.description: Criar um artigo completo para o LinkedIn que posiciona o profissional de saúde e bem-estar como referência — com profundidade técnica, linguagem executiva e argumento estratégico — para atrair clientes de maior valor, parcerias corporativas e convites para palestras e mentorias.

skills.name: bio-e-perfil-consultor-de-ia
skills.description: Criar a bio do LinkedIn, o headline, a apresentação do Instagram e os textos de perfil que comunicam de forma clara o que o consultor de IA faz — sem jargão técnico e sem soar como "mais um guru de tecnologia" — para que empresários entendam em 5 segundos o que ganham ao contratar ou seguir você. A bio certa atrai o cliente certo; a bio errada atrai curiosos.

skills.name: bio-e-perfil-que-converte
skills.description: Criar uma bio completa e estratégica para Instagram ou LinkedIn — com proposta de valor clara, prova de autoridade, público definido e CTA irresistível — para que o empreendedor solo pare de perder as pessoas que chegam no perfil sem seguir ou clicar, transformando o perfil em uma máquina de captação passiva que trabalha 24 horas por dia.

skills.name: bio-e-posicionamento-de-advogado-digital
skills.description: Criar a bio completa e a estratégia de posicionamento digital para advogados que produzem conteúdo nas redes sociais — definindo nicho, tom de voz, proposta de valor única e textos prontos para Instagram, LinkedIn e Google — para substituir bios genéricas por uma presença digital que atrai o cliente certo e comunica autoridade desde o primeiro contato.

skills.name: bio-e-posicionamento-digital
skills.description: Criar a bio, o posicionamento e a proposta de valor do perfil nas redes sociais — definindo claramente quem você é, para quem você fala, o que você oferece e por que alguém deveria te seguir. Uma bio forte é o primeiro filtro de conversão: é ela que transforma visitante em seguidor e seguidor em cliente.

skills.name: bio-e-posicionamento-para-instagram
skills.description: Criar a bio completa do Instagram — nome de perfil, frase de posicionamento, bullets de proposta de valor e CTA — com base no seu nicho, público e objetivo, para que cada visita ao perfil entenda em menos de 5 segundos o que você faz, para quem e por que vale a pena seguir. Uma bio bem construída converte visitantes em seguidores e seguidores em clientes.

skills.name: bio-profissional-para-saude-e-bem-estar
skills.description: Criar bios otimizadas e persuasivas para Instagram e LinkedIn de profissionais de saúde e bem-estar — que comunicam quem você atende, o que resolve e por que você — para transformar visitantes do perfil em seguidores qualificados e leads que chegam ao DM prontos para conversar.

skills.name: branding-e-identidade-do-escritorio-contabil
skills.description: Definir o branding completo do escritório contábil — posicionamento, tom de voz, proposta de valor única, nomenclatura dos serviços e diretrizes de comunicação — para que toda a presença digital (site, Instagram, LinkedIn, WhatsApp Business) transmita a mesma mensagem com profissionalismo e atraia o cliente certo, diferenciando o escritório dos concorrentes que parecem iguais.

skills.name: branding-e-narrativa-de-marca
skills.description: Criar a identidade de marca completa — com posicionamento, narrativa central, tom de voz, pilares de conteúdo e linha editorial — para uma perfumaria de nicho no TikTok e Instagram. Marca com narrativa forte converte melhor do que marca sem identidade porque o cliente compra o que a marca representa, não só o produto. No mercado de perfumaria, a narrativa é o produto.

skills.name: construtor-de-portfolio-e-autoridade-juridica
skills.description: Criar conteúdo estratégico de autoridade para o advogado freelancer — artigos, posts de LinkedIn, estudos de caso e materiais de portfólio — que demonstram expertise técnica para o público-alvo certo, atraem clientes qualificados organicamente e posicionam o profissional como referência no nicho, aumentando faturamento sem depender apenas de indicação ou prospecção ativa.

skills.name: conteudo-de-autoridade-no-mercado-imobiliario
skills.description: Criar conteúdo estratégico de posicionamento de autoridade para gestores, donos de imobiliária e especialistas no mercado imobiliário — com ganchos que param o scroll, estrutura que educa e argumentos que constroem credibilidade — para se tornar a referência que compradores, vendedores e corretores seguem, confiam e indicam, gerando leads por autoridade e não só por anúncio.

skills.name: copy-institucional-e-posicionamento-de-marca
skills.description: Criar textos institucionais — apresentação da empresa, about, tagline, missão, visão e proposta de valor — que comunicam claramente quem é a empresa, para quem ela existe e por que é diferente, para que o gestor tenha uma identidade de marca consistente para usar em propostas, site, LinkedIn, apresentações e qualquer material comercial, deixando de depender de descrições genéricas que não diferenciam de nenhum concorrente.

skills.name: criacao-de-comunidade-online-framework
skills.description: Projetar e lançar uma comunidade online do zero — definindo propósito, plataforma, regras, conteúdo inicial e estratégia de crescimento — para criar um espaço que gera valor real para os membros e se torna um ativo de longo prazo.

skills.name: curriculocv-otimizado
skills.description: Criar um currículo profissional otimizado para cada vaga — com headline impactante, experiências orientadas a resultados e palavras-chave certas — para passar pelos filtros de ATS, chamar atenção do recrutador em 6 segundos e conseguir a entrevista.

skills.name: estrategia-de-posicionamento-como-creator-de-ia
skills.description: Definir ou refinar o posicionamento estratégico como creator de conteúdo sobre IA na educação — com nicho preciso, proposta de valor única, voz autoral e diferencial claro em relação a outros creators do espaço — para que cada decisão de conteúdo reforce uma identidade coerente que atrai a audiência certa e constrói autoridade de longo prazo.

skills.name: estrutura-de-curso-digital-completo
skills.description: Criar a estrutura completa de um curso digital — do título ao conteúdo aula por aula — a partir de um tema informado. Inclui módulos organizados por progressão de aprendizagem, títulos de aula com ângulo certo, objetivos de cada módulo e sugestão de formato por aula, para que você saia do "tenho a ideia" para o "tenho o produto pronto para gravar" em minutos.

skills.name: estrutura-de-curso-online-modulos-e-aulas
skills.description: Projetar a estrutura completa de um curso online — definindo módulos, aulas, objetivos de aprendizagem, atividades práticas e sequência lógica — para criar uma experiência educacional que transforma o aluno e maximiza engajamento e conclusão.

skills.name: estrutura-de-palestra-framework-tedx
skills.description: Estruturar uma palestra impactante usando o framework TEDx — com abertura memorável, narrativa envolvente, ideia central poderosa e fechamento que inspira ação — para apresentações que emocionam, ensinam e são lembradas.

skills.name: estrutura-de-programa-de-mentoria-ou-consultoria
skills.description: Criar a estrutura completa de um programa de mentoria, consultoria ou treinamento — com módulos, sessões, entregas, metodologia e jornada do cliente — para que especialistas transformem seu conhecimento em um produto estruturado, escalável e fácil de comunicar. Programa bem estruturado vende mais porque o cliente entende o que vai receber, e entrega mais resultado porque o especialista sabe o que fazer em cada etapa.

skills.name: framework-de-facilitacao-de-workshops
skills.description: Criar roteiro completo e estrutura de facilitação para workshops presenciais ou online — com abertura, dinâmicas, conteúdo, momentos de reflexão e fechamento — para que consultores e especialistas em educação consigam facilitar qualquer workshop com profissionalismo e gerar impacto real nos participantes, mesmo sem experiência prévia em facilitação estruturada. O roteiro elimina a improvisação e garante consistência de entrega.

skills.name: framework-de-posicionamento-pessoal
skills.description: Definir o posicionamento estratégico completo do consultor, coach ou especialista — nicho, proposta de valor única, mensagem central e como comunicar tudo isso de forma clara e magnética. É o trabalho mais importante antes de qualquer conteúdo, proposta ou anúncio: sem posicionamento claro, tudo o mais é mais difícil. Com posicionamento forte, você atrai o cliente certo e afasta o cliente errado — e isso muda tudo na qualidade das vendas.

skills.name: framework-de-sessao-de-mentoria-11
skills.description: Estruturar sessões de mentoria 1:1 com um framework claro — abertura, diagnóstico, direcionamento e compromisso de ação — para que cada encontro gere valor tangível e progresso mensurável.

skills.name: framework-de-thought-leadership
skills.description: Construir um posicionamento de thought leadership (autoridade intelectual) — definindo área de expertise, ponto de vista único, sistema de conteúdo e estratégia de distribuição — para ser reconhecido como referência no seu mercado.

skills.name: framework-para-pensar-mais-fundo-sobre-ia
skills.description: Aplicar frameworks de pensamento estratégico — first principles, second-order thinking, inversão, cenários — a qualquer tema de IA agêntica ou educação, para que o creator vá além da superfície das discussões e produza análises com uma profundidade de raciocínio que a maioria dos criadores de conteúdo sobre tecnologia não consegue alcançar.

skills.name: linkedin-para-desenvolvedor-freelancer
skills.description: Otimizar o perfil do LinkedIn e criar uma estratégia de conteúdo que atrai clientes e oportunidades para o desenvolvedor freelancer — com headline que comunica valor, seção "Sobre" que converte visitantes em contatos, e plano de conteúdo que demonstra competência sem precisar de grande audiência — para transformar o LinkedIn de currículo estático em canal ativo de geração de oportunidades.

skills.name: otimizacao-de-perfil-do-linkedin
skills.description: Otimizar cada seção do perfil do LinkedIn — headline, sobre, experiências, destaques e skills — para atrair oportunidades profissionais, gerar conexões estratégicas e posicionar-se como referência na sua área.

skills.name: planejamento-estrategico-consultor-de-ia-solo
skills.description: Criar um plano estratégico trimestral completo para o negócio de consultoria de IA — com definição de nicho, metas de faturamento, canais de captação, produtos/serviços a desenvolver e rotina semanal de execução — que transforma a visão de "quero crescer" em um plano concreto semana a semana. O empreendedor solo precisa de um plano que caiba na realidade de uma pessoa fazendo tudo.

skills.name: planejamento-semanal-weekly-planning
skills.description: Criar um sistema de planejamento semanal estruturado — definindo prioridades, blocos de tempo, metas e revisão — para transformar semanas caóticas e reativas em semanas intencionais e produtivas.

skills.name: portfolio-e-cases-para-atrair-clientes
skills.description: Estruturar o portfólio e os cases de projetos de desenvolvimento de uma forma que comunica valor para o cliente — não só "veja o que fiz" mas "veja o problema que resolvi e o resultado que entreguei" — para ter um portfólio que atrai o cliente certo, justifica um preço mais alto e convence sem precisar de um pitch de vendas longo.

skills.name: portfolio-estrategico-para-iniciantes-em-branding
skills.description: Criar os textos e a estrutura de um portfólio profissional de branding — mesmo que você tenha poucos trabalhos reais ou apenas projetos fictícios — para parar de se desculpar pela falta de experiência e começar a se apresentar com autoridade desde o primeiro dia.

skills.name: posicionamento-de-autoridade-para-especialistas
skills.description: Criar o posicionamento estratégico completo de autoridade para consultores, coaches e especialistas — com nicho definido, proposta de valor única, método proprietário e narrativa de posicionamento — para que o mercado entenda exatamente para quem você é a melhor escolha, e para que clientes ideais cheguem com muito menos esforço de convencimento. Posicionamento forte é o que separa especialistas que brigam por preço dos que cobram premium.

skills.name: posicionamento-e-proposta-de-valor
skills.description: Definir ou refinar o posicionamento e a proposta de valor do negócio — quem você atende, qual problema você resolve de forma única e por que deveriam escolher você em vez da concorrência. O resultado é um posicionamento claro que aparece na bio, nas copies, na comunicação e nas vendas, atraindo o cliente certo e afastando quem não é o perfil ideal.

skills.name: posicionamento-e-proposta-de-valor-do-hub
skills.description: Criar o posicionamento estratégico e a proposta de valor clara para empreendedores que operam como hub — que coordenam parceiros e entregam soluções integradas — de forma que o mercado entenda o que você faz, por que é diferente de uma agência tradicional e por que o seu modelo vale o preço que você cobra. Posicionamento fraco faz cliente te tratar como intermediário; posicionamento forte te coloca como parceiro estratégico insubstituível.

skills.name: programa-de-mentoria-para-donos-de-imobiliaria
skills.description: Estruturar um programa completo de mentoria para donos de imobiliária — com diagnóstico inicial, trilha de sessões por tema, entregáveis por fase e ferramentas práticas para cada encontro — para que o mentor entregue uma experiência estruturada e de alto valor, e o mentorado saia de cada sessão com clareza sobre o próximo passo do seu negócio.

skills.name: proposta-de-treinamento-corporativo
skills.description: Criar propostas comerciais de treinamento corporativo completas e persuasivas — com diagnóstico, programa, metodologia, investimento e ROI projetado — para vender treinamentos in-company que resolvem problemas reais do negócio.

skills.name: skills-para-freelancers-precificacao-proposta-contrato
skills.description: Estruturar as bases profissionais de um freelancer — precificação correta, proposta comercial persuasiva e contrato de proteção — para deixar de improvisar, cobrar o que vale, fechar mais projetos e proteger-se legalmente.

skills.name: texto-institucional-e-apresentacao-da-empresa
skills.description: Criar textos institucionais completos — "Sobre nós", apresentação da empresa, missão/visão/valores e pitch de empresa — para uso em site, propostas comerciais, LinkedIn e materiais de marketing, de forma que a empresa seja apresentada com clareza, profissionalismo e posicionamento estratégico. Para gestores que nunca sabem o que escrever quando precisam descrever o próprio negócio.

skills.name: acessibilidade-web-wcag-checklist
skills.description: Auditar e corrigir problemas de acessibilidade em interfaces web seguindo as diretrizes WCAG 2.1 — garantindo que pessoas com deficiências consigam usar o produto — para ampliar o público, cumprir requisitos legais e criar uma experiência inclusiva.

skills.name: agente-de-ia-atendimento-via-whatsapp
skills.description: Criar o system prompt completo, o fluxo de conversa e as instruções de configuração de um agente de IA para atendimento automático via WhatsApp — que responde dúvidas, qualifica leads, agenda reuniões ou coleta informações de forma autônoma 24 horas por dia. O produto mais vendável na consultoria de implementação de IA para PMEs e o que gera o ROI mais visível para o cliente.

skills.name: autenticacao-e-autorizacao-implementacao
skills.description: Implementar um sistema completo de autenticação e autorização — com login, registro, tokens JWT, refresh tokens, roles e permissões — seguindo boas práticas de segurança, para proteger os recursos da aplicação.

skills.name: automacao-de-tarefas-repetitivas-do-negocio
skills.description: Identificar as tarefas repetitivas do negócio de freelancer que podem ser automatizadas com IA e ferramentas no-code — desde respostas de e-mail até geração de documentos, follow-ups e atualizações de projeto — e criar o plano de automação priorizado por tempo economizado, para que o único que faz tudo ganhe de volta horas por semana sem precisar contratar ninguém.

skills.name: automacao-no-code-n8n-e-zapier
skills.description: Criar o blueprint completo de um fluxo de automação no-code — descrevendo cada nó, gatilho, condição e ação em linguagem visual e passo a passo — para implementar no n8n ou Zapier sem precisar escrever código. Permite ao consultor de IA construir automações para si e para clientes usando ferramentas visuais, com um roteiro tão claro que qualquer pessoa consegue seguir.

skills.name: code-review-estruturado-checklist
skills.description: Realizar code reviews consistentes e construtivos usando um checklist estruturado — avaliando não só se o código funciona, mas se é legível, seguro, testável e manutenível — para elevar a qualidade do codebase e desenvolver a equipe.

skills.name: criacao-de-planilhas-inteligentes-com-ia
skills.description: Criar planilhas simples e úteis para controlar o negócio.

skills.name: debugger-sistematico-causa-raiz
skills.description: Aplicar um framework sistemático de debugging para isolar a causa raiz de bugs — ao invés de 'ficar tentando coisas' — reduzindo o tempo de resolução, evitando correções superficiais e documentando o processo para prevenir recorrência.

skills.name: design-de-api-restful-boas-praticas
skills.description: Projetar uma API RESTful seguindo boas práticas de design — com nomenclatura consistente, versionamento, tratamento de erros padronizado, paginação e autenticação — para criar APIs que são fáceis de usar, manter e escalar.

skills.name: dockerfile-otimizado-multi-stage
skills.description: Criar Dockerfiles otimizados usando multi-stage builds — reduzindo o tamanho da imagem final, melhorando a segurança e acelerando builds — para containers leves, rápidos de deployar e seguros para produção.

skills.name: estimativa-de-prazo-de-desenvolvimento
skills.description: Calcular estimativas de prazo realistas e defensáveis para projetos de desenvolvimento — com decomposição das funcionalidades em tarefas, estimativa de horas por tarefa, margem de risco e comunicação honesta com o cliente — para parar de prometer prazos impossíveis, parar de atrasar e nunca mais passar pela situação constrangedora de ter que pedir extensão de prazo porque não planejou direito.

skills.name: ia-como-engenheiro-de-software-pessoal
skills.description: Usar a IA como engenheiro de software pessoal — descrevendo em linguagem comum o que você quer automatizar ou construir e recebendo o código funcional, as instruções de instalação e o passo a passo de como fazer funcionar. Permite criar scripts de automação, integrações entre ferramentas e pequenos sistemas sem precisar saber programar, transformando ideias em código em minutos.

skills.name: modelagem-de-banco-de-dados-schema
skills.description: Projetar o schema de banco de dados relacional de forma estruturada — definindo tabelas, relacionamentos, índices e constraints — para criar uma base de dados que é performática, flexível para evoluir e correta desde o início.

skills.name: pipeline-cicd-github-actions
skills.description: Criar um pipeline de CI/CD completo com GitHub Actions — automatizando testes, build, linting e deploy — para que cada push/PR seja validado automaticamente e deploys aconteçam de forma segura e consistente.

skills.name: planejamento-de-sprint-solo
skills.description: Planejar sprints de desenvolvimento semanais ou quinzenais para freelancer solo — com backlog priorizado, estimativa de tarefas, metas de entrega e revisão de resultado — para ter sempre clareza sobre o que vai ser desenvolvido nesse período, evitar o "comecei 10 coisas e terminei nenhuma" e entregar projetos de forma previsível mesmo tocando múltiplos clientes.

skills.name: readme-profissional-template
skills.description: Criar um README completo e profissional para repositórios de código — com descrição clara, instruções de instalação, exemplos de uso e guia de contribuição — para que qualquer dev entenda, instale e contribua com o projeto em minutos.

skills.name: sistema-de-automacao-de-tarefas-com-ia
skills.description: Reduzir carga operacional usando IA.

skills.name: sistema-de-automacao-de-tarefas-repetitivas
skills.description: Reduzir tempo gasto em tarefas repetitivas.

skills.name: sistema-de-organizacao-para-iniciantes-em-ia
skills.description: Ajudar a usar IA de forma simples para ganhar produtividade.

skills.name: system-prompt-ia-personalizada-para-tarefa-especifica
skills.description: Criar system prompts completos e profissionais para configurar IAs personalizadas — seja para atendimento ao cliente, análise de documentos, geração de conteúdo, suporte interno ou qualquer outra tarefa — que funcionam de forma consistente, dentro do escopo definido e com o tom correto. skills.name: estruturacao-de-apresentacao-de-branding-para-cliente

skills.name: framework-de-posicionamento-premium-para-marca

skills.name: moodboard-e-curadoria-de-referencias-visuais

skills.name: one-pager-sales-sheet-b2b

skills.name: pesquisa-de-mercado-e-concorrencia-para-briefing-de-branding
skills.description: Estruturar pesquisa de mercado e análise de concorrência visual para projetos de branding — mapeando o que concorrentes comunicam visualmente, identificando padrões saturados no setor e localizando oportunidades de diferenciação — para que o designer entre na fase criativa com direção estratégica clara, não com uma tela em branco e intuição.

skills.name: proposta-comercial-de-projeto-de-branding-e-identidade-visual
skills.description: Criar propostas comerciais de branding e identidade visual que vão além do escopo e do preço — demonstrando o problema estratégico que o branding resolve, o valor percebido da entrega e o impacto no negócio do cliente — para que o designer feche mais projetos, com clientes que entendem o que estão comprando e respeitam o processo criativo.

skills.name: proposta-comercial-visual-b2b
skills.description: Criar propostas comerciais B2B com design profissional de alto impacto — estrutura visual que guia o olhar, hierarquia de informações que vende, e layout que transmite autoridade — para impressionar decisores e acelerar o fechamento.

skills.name: roteiro-de-case-study-de-projeto-de-branding
skills.description: Estruturar case studies de projetos de branding que vão além de mostrar o resultado visual — documentando o problema, o processo estratégico, as decisões criativas e o impacto — para que o designer construa portfólio que vende próximos projetos, não só portfólio bonito que ninguém sabe como foi feito.

skills.name: sales-deck-de-alto-impacto
skills.description: Criar um deck de vendas B2B com design estratégico — onde cada slide tem uma função clara na narrativa de venda, a hierarquia visual guia o olhar do decisor, e o design transmite autoridade para fechar negócios de ticket alto.

skills.name: texto-de-manifesto-e-personalidade-de-marca-para-cliente
skills.description: Criar manifestos de marca, declarações de posicionamento e textos de personalidade — que capturam a essência do negócio, definem o tom de voz e servem como guia para todas as decisões de comunicação — para que o designer entregue muito além do visual e o cliente tenha um ativo estratégico que orienta copy, conteúdo e presença da marca por anos.

skills.name: analise-critica-de-pecas-criativas
skills.description: Avaliar peças criativas com visão estratégica — identificando pontos fortes, fracos e melhorias práticas.

skills.name: analise-de-referencias-e-tendencias-criativas
skills.description: Transformar referências visuais em insights estratégicos — acelerando pesquisa e melhorando qualidade criativa.

skills.name: criacao-de-prompts-avancados-para-3d-e-design

skills.name: criacao-de-sistemas-de-campanha-multiformato
skills.description: Criar campanhas adaptáveis a múltiplos formatos — garantindo consistência e escala.

skills.name: criacao-de-sistemas-visuais-consistentes
skills.description: Criar sistemas visuais consistentes — garantindo coerência e escalabilidade na comunicação.

skills.name: direcao-criativa-para-campanhas-completas
skills.description: Criar direção criativa completa — com conceito, narrativa e execução — para campanhas consistentes e de alto impacto.

skills.name: estrutura-de-apresentacao-criativa-profissional
skills.description: Criar apresentações com narrativa clara e impacto visual — facilitando aprovação de projetos.

skills.name: framework-de-branding-estrategico
skills.description: Construir um branding estratégico completo — alinhando posicionamento, identidade e comunicação.

skills.name: framework-de-conceito-criativo-avancado

skills.description: Gerar direções de arte estratégicas e alinhadas ao conceito — facilitando execução visual consistente.

skills.name: framework-de-propostas-criativas-de-alto-impacto
skills.description: Criar propostas criativas com direção estratégica clara — unindo conceito, narrativa e execução visual para acelerar decisões e reduzir tempo de pesquisa.

skills.name: gerador-de-ideias-criativas-para-campanhas
skills.description: Gerar ideias criativas com base estratégica — reduzindo tempo de brainstorming e aumentando qualidade das campanhas.

skills.name: sistema-de-criacao-rapida-para-conteudo
skills.description: Criar conteúdo com velocidade e consistência usando estrutura clara.

skills.name: sistema-de-portfolio-estrategico
